member.name: T:Kdouja.Client.AarkamChunkMetadata
member.summary: Represents the cryptographic layout, payload size, index, and verification metadata of a single uploaded file chunk in the Aarkam storage network.

remarks.para: Instances of this class are generated after a successful chunk write operation. This object stores the metadata (such as the Initialization Vector and AEAD authentication tag) required to verify and decrypt the chunk on download. It is typically persisted within the file's index map or client database.

member.name: T:Kdouja.Client.Cryptography.ClientCrypto
member.summary: Provides high-throughput, zero-allocation cryptographic helper utilities for client-side key derivation, encryption, and decryption of storage chunks in the Aarkam distributed storage ecosystem.

remarks.para: In a zero-knowledge distributed storage architecture, client-side cryptography is critical to ensuring data privacy and integrity before transmission to untrusted storage nodes. Chunks are encrypted prior to leaving the client boundary, preventing exposure during gRPC transit or when persisted on disk.

Performance & Allocation Profile: Since encryption and key derivation are heavily executed on the critical hot path of high-volume data streams, this class utilizes and to avoid garbage collection (GC) pressure and heap allocations. Intermediate cryptographic states, initialization vectors, and derived keys are managed via stack allocation (stackalloc) or pooled memory.

Concurrency & Thread Safety: The class is fully stateless and thread-safe. All cryptographic operations are reentrant and do not lock or modify shared global state, allowing concurrent chunk processing in multi-threaded upload or download pipelines.

member.name: M:Kdouja.Client.Cryptography.ClientCrypto.DeriveChunkKey(System.Guid,System.Int32,System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte},System.Span{System.Byte})
member.summary: Derives a unique cryptographically secure 256-bit AES key for a specific chunk using HKDF-SHA256, bound to the file identifier, chunk index, and client-provided master key.

remarks.para: Key derivation prevents key reuse attacks across different chunks or files. In a distributed storage context with deduplication or multi-tenant architectures, unique per-chunk keys ensure that a breach of one chunk does not compromise the security of other chunks of the same file or cluster.

Hot-Path Efficiency: This method is highly optimized for the write/read pipeline. It constructs the HKDF context info parameter on the stack using a stack-allocated character buffer, formats guid and chunk index directly into the span without generating garbage strings, and derives the key directly into the caller-provided destination span.

member.param: The unique identifier of the file to which the chunk belongs. Used as salt/context bound.
The zero-based sequential index of the chunk. Prevents duplicate key derivation across different segments of the same file.
The client's 256-bit master key. Must contain exactly 32 bytes of high-entropy cryptographic material.
The destination buffer where the derived 32-byte AES key will be written. Must be at least 32 bytes in length.
member.exception: Thrown if the length is not 32 bytes, or if is less than 32 bytes.
Thrown if key derivation fails due to internal cryptographic provider errors.

member.summary: Encrypts the provided plaintext chunk using AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption, producing a ciphertext and an authentication tag.

remarks.para: Authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD) via AES-GCM guarantees both confidentiality and integrity of the stored chunks. Any tampering with the ciphertext during transmission or at rest on the storage nodes will cause decryption to fail.

Allocation Profile: To achieve zero-allocation encryption, this method accepts inputs and outputs as memory spans. It avoids allocating temporary arrays for ciphertext or tag data, making it ideal for high-throughput streaming pipelines. Under the hood, interacts directly with native OS cryptographic providers.

member.param: The read-only span containing the unencrypted chunk data.
The destination span where the encrypted chunk bytes will be written. Must be at least the same length as .
The 256-bit derived encryption key for the chunk (must be 32 bytes).
The 96-bit unique initialization vector (IV) or nonce (must be 12 bytes).
The destination span for the 128-bit authentication tag (must be 16 bytes).
member.exception: Thrown if the is not 32 bytes, the is not 12 bytes, the is not 16 bytes, or if is smaller than .
Thrown if the encryption operation fails due to cryptographic subsystem errors.

member.summary: Decrypts the provided ciphertext chunk using AES-256-GCM authenticated decryption, verifying integrity via the authentication tag.

remarks.para: In the storage engine read path, this decryption step serves as the final barrier. Integrity verification prevents corrupted or maliciously altered chunks from being reconstructed into the client application space, safeguarding against bit rot and man-in-the-middle attacks.

Performance and Allocation Profile: Operating entirely on spans allows this method to run with zero garbage collections in the hot read path. The decryption is performed in-place or to a pre-allocated/pooled plaintext buffer.

member.param: The read-only span containing the encrypted chunk data.
The destination span where the decrypted plaintext bytes will be written. Must be at least the same length as .
The 256-bit derived encryption key for the chunk (must be 32 bytes).
The 96-bit unique initialization vector (IV) used during encryption (must be 12 bytes).
The 128-bit authentication tag generated during encryption (must be 16 bytes).
member.exception: Thrown if the is not 32 bytes, the is not 12 bytes, the is not 16 bytes, or if is smaller than .
Thrown if the authentication tag verification fails (indicating data corruption/tampering) or if decryption fails.

member.name: T:Kdouja.Client.KdoujaClient
member.summary: Entry point for the Aarkam client-side SDK. Coordinates high-throughput, zero-allocation, and zero-knowledge client-side encryption, chunking, and streaming data transmission to and from the Aarkam distributed storage cluster via gRPC.

remarks.para: In a zero-knowledge distributed storage architecture, data privacy and integrity must be guaranteed prior to sending data to untrusted storage nodes. The client splits files into discrete, fixed-size chunks, derives unique keys for each chunk using HKDF-SHA256, encrypts them using authenticated ciphers (AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305), and streams them using gRPC streaming.

Performance & Allocation Profile: Since block processing is executed on the critical hot path of massive file streams, this client employs to lease large chunk buffers, avoiding frequent LOH (Large Object Heap) allocations and GC pressure. Cryptographic parameters (such as derived keys, IVs, and tags) are handled on the stack using stackalloc to avoid heap allocations.

Concurrency & Lifespan: While instances of are thread-safe and can manage multiple concurrent streaming calls, the underlying should be reused across the application's lifespan to avoid connection renegotiation overhead.

member.name: M:Kdouja.Client.KdoujaClient.UploadFileAsync(System.Guid,System.IO.Stream,System.Byte[],System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Uploads a file by chunking it, encrypting each chunk with derived keys on the fly, and streaming the encrypted chunks to the Aarkam Gateway.

remarks.para: Data is streamed to the gateway via a gRPC bidirectional stream, making it suitable for extremely large files without consuming substantial client memory. The input stream is read sequentially, buffered using rented arrays from , and encrypted chunk by chunk.

Security details: Keys derived via HKDF-SHA256 ensure that if one chunk's key is compromised, other chunk keys remain secure. Initialization vectors are filled using a cryptographically secure random number generator ().

member.param: The unique identifier of the file. Used as part of the salt for chunk key derivation.
The readable input stream containing the file data to upload.
The client's 256-bit master key (must be exactly 32 bytes in length).
Optional. The algorithm used for chunk encryption (e.g., "AES-256-GCM" or "ChaCha20-Poly1305"). Defaults to "AES-256-GCM".
A token to monitor for cancellation requests.
member.returns: A representing the asynchronous upload operation.
member.exception: Thrown if is null or is null.
Thrown if the is not exactly 32 bytes, or if is not readable.
Thrown if an I/O error occurs reading or if the Gateway fails to write the chunk.
Thrown if encryption fails.

member.summary: Downloads a file by fetching chunks sequentially from the Gateway, verifying their integrity, decrypting them, and writing plaintext to the output stream.

remarks.para: This method requests chunks sequentially, matching the order they were uploaded. Verification of the AEAD authentication tag (AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305) is completed before plaintext is written to the destination stream. If tampering or corruption is detected, decryption will fail immediately.

member.param: The unique identifier of the file to download.
The total number of chunks containing the file.
The writable destination stream where plaintext will be written.
The client's 256-bit master key (must be exactly 32 bytes in length).
Optional. The algorithm used during encryption (e.g., "AES-256-GCM" or "ChaCha20-Poly1305").
A token to monitor for cancellation requests.
member.returns: A representing the asynchronous download operation.
member.exception: Thrown if is null or is null.
Thrown if the is not exactly 32 bytes or is less than 0.
Thrown if a requested chunk cannot be found on the storage cluster.
Thrown if writing to the output stream fails or if a network error occurs.
Thrown if integrity tag verification fails, indicating corruption or tampering.
